page: Microsoft Azure D96als_v6 is an x86_64 virtual machine from the Dalv6 family running on Microsoft Hyper-V. Powered by AMD processors, this instance provides 96 dedicated vCPUs alongside 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include dedicated GPU accelerators.

In terms of storage and connectivity, the instance comes with no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes, and is capable of attaching Premium Storage. There are zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses provided by default. The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio creates a low-memory footprint relative to standard general-purpose offerings, making the system suitable for compute-heavy profiles that do not require high memory per thread.

From an architectural and cost-efficiency perspective, the D96als_v6 allows organizations requiring high core density to scale parallel processing without bearing the overhead of surplus RAM capacity. Key tradeoffs include the absence of integrated local ephemeral storage and the constrained memory allocation per core. This configuration aligns with multi-threaded, CPU-bound workloads such as code compilation, batch compute processing, continuous integration and delivery pipelines, and distributed worker nodes.
